Closes #3351

## What changed

**One shared budget (R3351000).** Moving faces, tile auras, backdrops, particles and tilt now share `PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET` (6) on a phone, with `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` (120) beside the existing 50 ms mean budget, both in [constants.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/constants.ts).

**Named shed order.** New [shed.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/shed.ts) publishes stages 0–3. The [director](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/director.ts) sheds one stage per slow window (same trip as the existing cap halve, whose B34 behavior is unchanged) and recovers one per healthy set: stage 1 halves burst/projectile/shot emission (bursts keep ≥1 mote); stage 2 halves far-aura and tile mote budgets ([AuraLayer](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/aura/AuraLayer.tsx), [TileAura](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/aura/TileAura.tsx)); stage 3 stills every face past the pointer's own ([motionSlots](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/cards/motionSlots.ts), rank kept for recovery). Set-piece beats are DOM cues with no particle counts, so they never shed. [FxLayer](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/apps/web/src/fx/FxLayer.tsx) feeds one passive pointer listener into the store.

**Scenario + coverage.** New `e2e/cypress/component/fx-phone-living-game.cy.tsx`: five art-first Units (Silly Silas, Felinor Fiender, Tylannt, Paragon-X, Prototype-X2), an Anomaly backdrop, a launched Starship and a ten-card hand with a tilted Mythic, played through anomaly cast, Mythic takeover, Starship launch, 8-gun broadside, Battleship arrival, Ceaseless Void fold, hand-to-tile flight and riffle at 390x844, 360x780 and 844x390 under 4x CDP throttling, asserting mean ≤ 50 ms and worst ≤ 120 ms, plus a deterministic shed-order test. `card-fullscreen.cy.tsx` gains a long-press test over 5 board faces + 10 hand cards (inspect everywhere, fullscreen where R3345000 allows; opponent Mythic asserts fullscreen stays shut). Ruling [R3351000](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/spec/rulings/R3351000.md), [pending/3351.md](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-3351/spec/pending/3351.md).

## How it was tested

- `vitest run` on 10 files (shed, director, constants, FxLayer, stage, AuraLayer, TileAura, motionSlots, artLive, animations.flavor): **224/224 pass**, including 9 new R3351000 tests; B34/B41 capacity semantics untouched.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck` (43 fixtures OK), `typecheck:component`, `eslint` on all touched files, `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok (1863 rulings, 4808 proofs); `catalog check`, `patches check`: ok.
- **Not run here**: the two Cypress component specs and e2e 46/47 — this machine has Chrome and the Cypress binary but no Xvfb and no sudo, so no browser runs; CI exercises them. The specs are built verbatim from proven patterns in `fx-phone-frame.cy.tsx` and typecheck clean.

## Decisions the task did not settle

- The plan put aura/face shedding in `FxLayer`, but `Game` renders `FxLayer` and `AuraLayer` as siblings, so the layer has no handle on them: the director scales emission at `fire()` and the layers read the published level. Same observable order, correct seam.
- Stage 3 keeps only the hovered face: the slot allocator has no face geometry, and hovered-first ranking already means the hovered face is nearest the pointer. "Far" likewise means "whose box is not under the pointer" (AuraLayer measures boxes); TileAura sheds with the far set (it measures none). The ruling states both plainly.
- Test titles use full `R3351000` (the plan's `R3351` shorthand would fail `spec check` as an unknown ruling).
- The cy shed test forces stages through the published store instead of manufacturing slow frames: deterministic in-browser proof of the order; the slow-window trip itself is pinned in `director.test.ts`. Worst-frame retries like the mean (noise only adds time).
- Broadside runs at slowest speed, then restores full speed; five units are hardcoded verified defIds, not a catalog search.
- No owning-part fixes: nothing measurable failed here (no browser); e2e 46/47 are unaffected (FX-only diff, no layout/menu/controls touched) but unrun here.

## Look twice

- `director.ts` recover condition gained `|| shedStage() > 0` so shed recovers even if the cap is already home; lockstep with the cap holds in all existing tests.
- `motionSlots.ts` `active = wanted && (!still || hovered)`: tokens/ages survive shed so recovery reclaims old rank (covered by test).
- New spec's moment retry resets to the plain board first — replaying identical events would otherwise diff empty and sample an idle board.
- `card-fullscreen` mount passes `wearCosmetics` (as hotseat does); without it no board face is "worn" and fullscreen could never open.

```text
# #3351: Patch: the living game on a phone: a pass at 390x844 and on a throttled CPU over every look, animation and sound #3330 adds, with one budget they share
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

## What it does

Part of #3330. Blocked by #3339, #3340, #3341, #3342, #3344, #3345, #3347, #3348, #3334, #3336, #3337 and #3338.

The owner asked that all of this look good on a phone too, not only on a computer. Each part under #3330 checks itself at 390x844. This part checks them **together**, on the board a real game produces, and sets the one budget they share.

### What it should be

1. **A full-board scenario at phone size.** Add a component spec (`e2e/cypress/component/`) or e2e spec that plays, at 390x844, 360x780 and a phone on its side, with the CPU throttled 4x (Chrome DevTools Protocol `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`). The board holds:
   - five art-first Units, two Legendary and one Mythic among them, with tile auras;
   - an Anomaly's backdrop;
   - a launched Starship;
   - a hand of ten, one tilted.

   Through it play a Mythic takeover, a Starship launch and broadside, a Drone Battleship arrival, a Terminus set piece, a hand-to-tile flight and a riffle, and measure frame times throughout.
2. **One shared budget.** Moving faces, tile auras, backdrops, particles and tilt share one budget on a phone, `PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET` in `fx/constants.ts`. The adaptive cap (`FX_ADAPT_*`, `director.ts`) sheds in a named order when frames run long:
   - motes first;
   - then far auras;
   - then the moving faces furthest from the pointer;
   - never a set piece's main beats.

   The mean frame stays under `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS`, and the worst under `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` (proposed and ruled).
3. **Fixes.** Fix what the scenario finds in the part that owns it. If the fix belongs to a part still open, write a short note on that part instead.
4. **Layout.** The one-screen rule (R1581000) and the tap areas (R2122000) hold with all of it on: e2e `46` and `47`, plus a long-press check that inspect and the full-screen view (#3345) open from every board face and hand card.

## Acceptance

- The scenario runs at the three sizes under 4x throttling, within `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` mean and `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` worst.
- The shed order is tested: a forced slow frame sheds motes first and set-piece beats never.
- e2e `46`, `47` and the long-press check pass with every part's features on.
- The pull request lists each finding and where it was fixed or noted.
- Any ruling is in this issue's block, with the §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<this issue>.md`. The web tests, `typecheck`, `eslint` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.

# #3351: Patch: the living game on a phone: a pass at 390x844 and on a throttled CPU over every look, animation and sound #3330 adds, with one budget they share
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

## What it does

Part of #3330. Blocked by #3339, #3340, #3341, #3342, #3344, #3345, #3347, #3348, #3334, #3336, #3337 and #3338.

The owner asked that all of this look good on a phone too, not only on a computer. Each part under #3330 checks itself at 390x844. This part checks them **together**, on the board a real game produces, and sets the one budget they share.

### What it should be

1. **A full-board scenario at phone size.** Add a component spec (`e2e/cypress/component/`) or e2e spec that plays, at 390x844, 360x780 and a phone on its side, with the CPU throttled 4x (Chrome DevTools Protocol `Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`). The board holds:
   - five art-first Units, two Legendary and one Mythic among them, with tile auras;
   - an Anomaly's backdrop;
   - a launched Starship;
   - a hand of ten, one tilted.

   Through it play a Mythic takeover, a Starship launch and broadside, a Drone Battleship arrival, a Terminus set piece, a hand-to-tile flight and a riffle, and measure frame times throughout.
2. **One shared budget.** Moving faces, tile auras, backdrops, particles and tilt share one budget on a phone, `PHONE_MOTION_BUDGET` in `fx/constants.ts`. The adaptive cap (`FX_ADAPT_*`, `director.ts`) sheds in a named order when frames run long:
   - motes first;
   - then far auras;
   - then the moving faces furthest from the pointer;
   - never a set piece's main beats.

   The mean frame stays under `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS`, and the worst under `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` (proposed and ruled).
3. **Fixes.** Fix what the scenario finds in the part that owns it. If the fix belongs to a part still open, write a short note on that part instead.
4. **Layout.** The one-screen rule (R1581000) and the tap areas (R2122000) hold with all of it on: e2e `46` and `47`, plus a long-press check that inspect and the full-screen view (#3345) open from every board face and hand card.

## Acceptance

- The scenario runs at the three sizes under 4x throttling, within `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS` mean and `FX_PHONE_FRAME_WORST_MS` worst.
- The shed order is tested: a forced slow frame sheds motes first and set-piece beats never.

- Any ruling is in this issue's block, with the §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/<this issue>.md`. The web tests, `typecheck`, `eslint` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
